question: What does the launcher add/remove ABI consume, and how does it obtain the registered app descriptor? (CAN-APP-002/003)
prototype_hypothesis: app_launcher_add(u16 app_id) -> implementation-defined int; app_launcher_del(u16 app_id) -> implementation-defined int. app_launcher_add resolves the already-installed 64-byte app descriptor through off_200EB058[1](app_id), then passes that descriptor to load_app_info.
callsite_evidence: sub_C527E38 quickapp_register_app first calls off_200EB060(descriptor, &page, 1), then calls sub_C4F2BDC with the u16 app ID still in R0; its earlier lookup also calls off_200EB058[1](a1), where a1 is the app ID
sub_C5B7DE0 reinstall_app_cb obtains a descriptor through off_200EB058[3](package_name), then calls sub_C4F2BDC with the descriptor's u16 field at +16 loaded into R0 by the surrounding path
app_launcher_add = sub_C4F2BDC: its entry R0 is forwarded unchanged to off_200EB058[1]; the returned descriptor is then forwarded unchanged to sub_C4F2898 load_app_info
load_app_info = sub_C4F2898: rejects null, missing icon (+12==0), and hidden (+60&1); warns when flags +18 has bit2; builds a 24-byte runtime launcher record
app_launcher_del = sub_C4F2CC4: finds and removes the runtime launcher record by u16 app ID
control_flow_evidence: sub_C4F2BDC entry has no instruction replacing R0 before BLX off_200EB058[1], proving its public input is the registry lookup key rather than a descriptor pointer
load_app_info reads descriptor +8 package name, +12 icon resource, +16 u16 app ID, +18 flags, +28 callback, and +60 hidden bit
descriptor +28 is invoked both with (descriptor, empty-string) for the 'App is (%s, %s)' log and with (descriptor) to populate runtime record +4; the exact semantic/return contract remains unresolved
ownership_analysis: app_launcher_add borrows only the u16 ID. The installed app registry owns a deep-copied 64-byte descriptor. load_app_info creates a separate launcher record that borrows descriptor string pointers and stores the callback result at record+4; removal frees the launcher record and its resolved handle according to launcher cleanup.
unsafe_assumptions: the descriptor +28 callback has inconsistent observed call arity and is not safe to expose until device-probed
the return values of app_launcher_add/app_launcher_del are log/cleanup results rather than a proven boolean success contract
the icon resource format and callback result ownership are not yet recovered
calling app_launcher_add before app_install has registered the descriptor cannot work
recommended_probe: Install one synthetic descriptor through the restricted app_install binding, verify registry lookup by u16 ID, then invoke app_launcher_add(u16) on the launcher owner thread and observe creation/removal without interpreting its return as boolean.
